boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing Terre Haute destinations on distinct corridors for art, history, learning, and outdoor time.

cards.title: Sheldon Swope Art Museum
cards.subtitle: South 7th Street corridor
cards.notes: Head to 25 South 7th Street to view changing exhibitions and selections from the museum’s American-art collection.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown museum with a substantial American-art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Swope holds nearly 2,500 American artworks and states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: 25 South 7th Street; listed hours are Tuesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.

cards.title: Terre Haute Children’s Museum
cards.subtitle: Wabash Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit 727 Wabash Avenue for three floors of hands-on science exhibits; check the museum page before planning around closures.
cards.short_summary: Interactive science and play exhibits in downtown Terre Haute.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum describes three floors of science, learning, and play, including Water Works and a ropes course.
cards.access_notes: Admission is ticketed; current entry hours and prices are posted by the museum.

cards.title: Vigo County History Center
cards.subtitle: Wabash Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 929 Wabash Avenue to work through three floors of artifacts and exhibits about Vigo County’s past and present.
cards.short_summary: A three-floor local-history museum in the Wabash Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The History Center says its three floors and 34,000 square feet connect visitors with Vigo County people, stories, and artifacts.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the site lists paid admission.

cards.entity_name: Vigo County Public Library Main Library
cards.title: Vigo County Public Library Main Library
cards.subtitle: Poplar Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Main Library at 680 Poplar Street for a daytime reset, research stop, or a look at the public program calendar.
cards.short_summary: A central public-library stop with long weekday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Vigo County Public Library lists its Main Library at 680 Poplar Street and lists Monday–Thursday hours of 8 a.m.–8 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Listed Main Library hours: Mon–Thu 8 a.m.–8 p.m., Fri 8 a.m.–6 p.m., Sat 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Sun 1–5 p.m.

cards.entity_name: CANDLES Holocaust Museum and Education Center
cards.title: CANDLES Holocaust Museum and Education Center
cards.subtitle: South Third Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan a focused museum visit at 1532 South Third Street; the organization recommends its material for upper-grade students and older.
cards.short_summary: A Holocaust education museum with public visiting hours.
cards.evidence_claim: CANDLES identifies its Terre Haute location, public Thursday–Saturday hours, and Holocaust-focused educational mission.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Thursday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; the museum lists student admission pricing.

cards.title: Fairbanks Park
cards.subtitle: Dresser Drive and Wabash River corridor
cards.notes: Use the city park map to orient a riverfront walk and locate the named park features along the Wabash River edge.
cards.short_summary: A named riverfront park documented on the City of Terre Haute map.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Terre Haute’s Fairbanks Park map identifies Fairbanks Park and the Wabash River.
cards.source_title: City of Terre Haute Fairbanks Park Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; check local conditions and any event notices before visiting.

cards.title: Deming Park
cards.subtitle: Fruitridge Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Start at the Fruitridge Avenue side and use the city map to find the Holly Arboretum, ponds, playground, and miniature train.
cards.short_summary: A large city park with mapped gardens, ponds, and recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Terre Haute’s Deming Park map labels the Holly Arboretum, Oakley Playground, ponds, and Spirit of Terre Haute Miniature Train.
cards.source_title: City of Terre Haute Deming Park Map
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park destination; individual amenities may have separate seasonal operations.

cards.title: Dobbs Park Nature Center
cards.subtitle: East Poplar Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the East Poplar Street entrance for a nature-focused outing; keep to designated trails and explore the preserve respectfully.
cards.short_summary: A city nature-center destination beside a state nature preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Indiana DNR identifies Dobbs Park Nature Center at 5170 Poplar Street in Terre Haute, adjacent to Dobbs Memorial Nature Preserve.
cards.source_title: Indiana DNR Dobbs Memorial Nature Preserve
cards.access_notes: Nature-center and preserve visit; follow posted rules and trail guidance.

cards.title: Fowler Park
cards.subtitle: East Oregon Church Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a picnic or plan a daylight trail walk at 3000 East Oregon Church Road, where the county lists lakes and a pioneer village.
cards.short_summary: A county park combining trails, lakes, and historic structures.
cards.evidence_claim: Vigo County Parks lists Fowler Park amenities including lakes, trails, a covered bridge, pioneer village, and working gristmill.
cards.access_notes: County park at 3000 East Oregon Church Road; amenities and seasonal uses vary.

cards.entity_name: Wabashiki Fish & Wildlife Area – Dewey Point
cards.title: Wabashiki Fish & Wildlife Area – Dewey Point
cards.subtitle: East National Avenue corridor, West Terre Haute
cards.notes: Use the Dewey Point access at 110 East National Avenue for the observatory and trailhead; review DNR notices before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A free DNR wetland and birding access point across the river.
cards.evidence_claim: Indiana DNR lists Dewey Point at 110 East National Avenue, free admission, a birding-trail stop, and the Dewey Point–Wabashiki Trail.
cards.source_title: Indiana DNR: Wabashiki Fish & Wildlife Area
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; property access is listed as 24/7, while some activities have specific rules or seasonal restrictions.
